## ED PHYSICIAN NOTE - CLINICAL ASSESSMENT 

PATIENT Dax Vance 

DOB 04/12/2001 

MRN 940-2281-A 

DATE OF SERVICE 09/04/2023 

## Presenting History 

Patient is a 22-year-old male driver of a sedan involved in high-speed, multi-vehicle side-impact MVA at 18:45 tonight. Requires extraction due to vehicle frame distortion. Patient is alert but cooperative only intermittently, demonstrating mild combativeness and an obvious odor of alcohol. Confirmed consumption of 4 beers pre-crash. Complaining of 10/10 severe pain in left arm, severe cervical neck pain, lower back discomfort, and a heavy headache. 

## Physical Examination 

HEENT: Active 2cm superficial laceration over left parietal scalp, mild tenderness to palpation, pupils equal and reactive. 
Neck: Severe tenderness over C4-C7 vertebrae. Prominent muscle spasm in bilateral trapezius. Pain aggravated by any passive movement. Cervical collar maintained. 
Cardiovascular / Pulmonary: Tachycardic but regular. Lungs clear bilaterally. 
Left Upper Extremity: Gross deformity of left humerus mid-shaft with an open skin puncture measuring 2.5cm, bone fragment visible. Active bleeding present but partially controlled with sterile pressure dressings. Severe swelling and visible spiral deformity of distal radius. Left radial pulse is 1+ (weak) and capillary refill is delayed at 3.5 seconds. Distal sensation is moderately decreased in the radial nerve distribution. 
Left Lower Extremity: Focal bruising and tenderness over anterior left knee, range of motion guarded. 
Back: Mild paraspinal lumbar tenderness, no step-offs. 

## Assessment & Plan 

1. Left humerus mid-shaft open/compound fracture. 
2. Left distal radius spiral fracture. 
3. Acute cervicalgia with high suspicion of ligamentous or disc injury. 
4. Acute scalp laceration. 
5. Ethanol intoxication. Consult Orthopedic Surgery (Dr. Myrtle Turner) immediately for emergency open reduction and internal fixation (ORIF). Initiate IV antibiotics (Ancef) and aggressive pain management. Obtain emergency X-rays of left arm, C-spine, and lumbar spine.

ACCESSION	RAD-2023-8812 Exam date 09/04/2023
INTERPRETING MD	Dr. Elizabeth Foster, MD



## TECHNIQUE 

Three-view radiographs of the left humerus and left forearm. 

## FINDINGS 

There is an displaced, mid-shaft fracture of the left humerus with a lateral bone fragment piercing through adjacent subcutaneous tissue (open compound presentation). Substantial overriding of fracture fragments by 2.2 cm. Additionally, there is a complex spiral fracture of the distal one-third of the radius, with intra-articular extension. Mild posterior displacement of the distal radial fragments. Moderate swelling in surrounding soft tissues. 

## IMPRESSION 

1. Highly unstable compound mid-shaft humerus fracture with significant overriding. 2. Displaced spiral fracture of the distal radius with intra-articular extension.

EXAMINATION	X-ray Cervical Spine
ACCESSION	RAD-2023-8813 . Exam date 09/04/2023
INTERPRETING MD	Dr. Elizabeth Foster, MD



## TECHNIQUE 

AP, lateral, and odontoid views of the cervical spine. 

## FINDINGS 

There is narrowing of the C5-C6 intervertebral disc space with osteophytic lipping. Mild retrolisthesis of C5 on C6. A prominent 6mm posterior/paracentral disc bulge is visualized at the C5-C6 level, compressing the anterior thecal sac. There is moderate prevertebral soft tissue swelling from C4 through C6. No acute vertebral body fractures identified. 

## IMPRESSION 

1. C5-C6 disc narrowing and significant posterior disc bulge measuring 6mm, producing moderate central canal narrowing. 2. Prevertebral soft tissue swelling, consistent with acute flexion/extension trauma. Clinical correlation with prior records is advised as the onset date of the bulge is inconclusive.
